Why Gulls Follow the Ferries

Gulls that nest near the harbour have learned that the ferry stirs up small fish with its propellers, and they follow the boat out of the harbour on almost every crossing during the breeding season, when their chicks need the most food.

The birds also learned the timetable. Observers counted far more gulls waiting on the breakwater in the minutes before a departure than at any other time of day, and the number dropped as soon as the last ferry of the evening had left the harbour.

Ferry crews say that the gulls ignore the smaller boats entirely, which suggests that the birds tell the vessels apart by their size or by the sound of their engines rather than following any boat that happens to leave the harbour.
